00121 Some of the current weaknesses (which we aim to address in the future) includes: 00122 00123 - Doesn't look fancy. 00124 - Limited layout features, intricate layouts are typically crafted in code. 00125 00126 00127 CONTROLS GUIDE 00128 ============== 00129 00130 - MOUSE CONTROLS 00131 - Mouse wheel: Scroll vertically. 00132 - SHIFT+Mouse wheel: Scroll horizontally. 00133 - Click [X]: Close a window, available when 'bool* p_open' is passed to ImGui::Begin(). 00134 - Click ^, Double-Click title: Collapse window. 00135 - Drag on corner/border: Resize window (double-click to auto fit window to its contents). 00136 - Drag on any empty space: Move window (unless io.ConfigWindowsMoveFromTitleBarOnly = true). 00137 - Left-click outside popup: Close popup stack (right-click over underlying popup: Partially close popup stack). 00138 00139 - TEXT EDITOR 00140 - Hold SHIFT or Drag Mouse: Select text. 00141 - CTRL+Left/Right: Word jump. 00142 - CTRL+Shift+Left/Right: Select words. 00143 - CTRL+A or Double-Click: Select All. 00144 - CTRL+X, CTRL+C, CTRL+V: Use OS clipboard. 00145 - CTRL+Z, CTRL+Y: Undo, Redo. 00146 - ESCAPE: Revert text to its original value. 00147 - On OSX, controls are automatically adjusted to match standard OSX text editing 2ts and behaviors. 00148 00149 - KEYBOARD CONTROLS 00150 - Basic: 00151 - Tab, SHIFT+Tab Cycle through text editable fields. 00152 - CTRL+Tab, CTRL+Shift+Tab Cycle through windows. 00153 - CTRL+Click Input text into a Slider or Drag widget. 00154 - Extended features with `io.ConfigFlags |= ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard`: 00155 - Tab, SHIFT+Tab: Cycle through every items. 00156 - Arrow keys Move through items using directional navigation. Tweak value. 00157 - Arrow keys + Alt, Shift Tweak slower, tweak faster (when using arrow keys). 00158 - Enter Activate item (prefer text input when possible). 00159 - Space Activate item (prefer tweaking with arrows when possible). 00160 - Escape Deactivate item, leave child window, close popup. 00161 - Page Up, Page Down Previous page, next page. 00162 - Home, End Scroll to top, scroll to bottom. 00163 - Alt Toggle between scrolling layer and menu layer. 00164 - CTRL+Tab then Ctrl+Arrows Move window. Hold SHIFT to resize instead of moving. 00165 - Output when ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard set, 00166 - io.WantCaptureKeyboard flag is set when keyboard is claimed. 00167 - io.NavActive: true when a window is focused and it doesn't have the ImGuiWindowFlags_NoNavInputs flag set. 00168 - io.NavVisible: true when the navigation cursor is visible (usually goes to back false when mouse is used). 00169 00170 - GAMEPAD CONTROLS 00171 - Enable with 'io.ConfigFlags |= ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableGamepad'. 00172 - Particularly useful to use Dear ImGui on a console system (e.g. PlayStation, Switch, Xbox) without a mouse! 00173 - Download controller mapping PNG/PSD at http://dearimgui.com/controls_sheets 00174 - Backend support: backend needs to: 00175 - Set 'io.BackendFlags |= ImGuiBackendFlags_HasGamepad' + call io.AddKeyEvent/AddKeyAnalogEvent() with ImGuiKey_Gamepad_XXX keys. 00176 - For analog values (0.0f to 1.0f), backend is responsible to handling a dead-zone and rescaling inputs accordingly. 00177 Backend code will probably need to transform your raw inputs (such as e.g. remapping your 0.2..0.9 raw input range to 0.0..1.0 imgui range, etc.). 00178 - BEFORE 1.87, BACKENDS USED TO WRITE TO io.NavInputs[]. This is now obsolete. Please call io functions instead! 00179 - If you need to share inputs between your game and the Dear ImGui interface, the easiest approach is to go all-or-nothing, 00180 with a buttons combo to toggle the target. Please reach out if you think the game vs navigation input sharing could be improved. 00181 00182 - REMOTE INPUTS SHARING & MOUSE EMULATION 00183 - PS4/PS5 users: Consider emulating a mouse cursor with DualShock touch pad or a spare analog stick as a mouse-emulation fallback. 00184 - Consoles/Tablet/Phone users: Consider using a Synergy 1.x server (on your PC) + run examples/libs/synergy/uSynergy.c (on your console/tablet/phone app) 00185 in order to share your PC mouse/keyboard. 00186 - See https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/wiki/Useful-Extensions#remoting for other remoting solutions. 00187 - On a TV/console system where readability may be lower or mouse inputs may be awkward, you may want to set the ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableSetMousePos flag. 00188 Enabling ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableSetMousePos + ImGuiBackendFlags_HasSetMousePos instructs Dear ImGui to move your mouse cursor along with navigation movements. 00189 When enabled, the NewFrame() function may alter 'io.MousePos' and set 'io.WantSetMousePos' to notify you that it wants the mouse cursor to be moved. 00190 When that happens your backend NEEDS to move the OS or underlying mouse cursor on the next frame. Some of the backends in examples/ do that. 00191 (If you set the NavEnableSetMousePos flag but don't honor 'io.WantSetMousePos' properly, Dear ImGui will misbehave as it will see your mouse moving back & forth!) 00192 (In a setup when you may not have easy control over the mouse cursor, e.g. uSynergy.c doesn't expose moving remote mouse cursor, you may want 00193 to set a boolean to ignore your other external mouse positions until the external source is moved again.) 00194 00195 00196 PROGRAMMER GUIDE 00197 ================ 00198 00199 READ FIRST 00200 ---------- 00201 - Remember to check the wonderful Wiki (https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/wiki) 00202 - Your code creates the UI every frame of your application loop, if your code doesn't run the UI is gone! 00203 The UI can be highly dynamic, there are no construction or destruction steps, less superfluous 00204 data retention on your side, less state duplication, less state synchronization, fewer bugs. 00205 - Call and read ImGui::ShowDemoWindow() for demo code demonstrating most features. 00206 Or browse https://pthom.github.io/imgui_manual_online/manual/imgui_manual.html for interactive web version. 00207 - The library is designed to be built from sources. Avoid pre-compiled binaries and packaged versions. See imconfig.h to configure your build. 00208 - Dear ImGui is an implementation of the IMGUI paradigm (immediate-mode graphical user interface, a term coined by Casey Muratori). 00209 You can learn about IMGUI principles at http://www.johno.se/book/imgui.html, http://mollyrocket.com/861 & more links in Wiki. 00210 - Dear ImGui is a "single pass" rasterizing implementation of the IMGUI paradigm, aimed at ease of use and high-performances. 00211 For every application frame, your UI code will be called only once. This is in contrast to e.g. Unity's implementation of an IMGUI, 00212 where the UI code is called multiple times ("multiple passes") from a single entry point. There are pros and cons to both approaches. 00213 - Our origin is on the top-left. In axis aligned bounding boxes, Min = top-left, Max = bottom-right. 00214 - Please make sure you have asserts enabled (IM_ASSERT redirects to assert() by default, but can be redirected). 00215 If you get an assert, read the messages and comments around the assert. 00216 - This codebase aims to be highly optimized: 00217 - A typical idle frame should never call malloc/free. 00218 - We rely on a maximum of constant-time or O(N) algorithms. Limiting searches/scans as much as possible. 00219 - We put particular energy in making sure performances are decent with typical "Debug" build settings as well. 00220 Which mean we tend to avoid over-relying on "zero-cost abstraction" as they aren't zero-cost at all. 00221 - This codebase aims to be both highly opinionated and highly flexible: 00222 - This code works because of the things it choose to solve or not solve. 00223 - C++: this is a pragmatic C-ish codebase: we don't use fancy C++ features, we don't include C++ headers, 00224 and ImGui:: is a namespace. We rarely use member functions (and when we did, I am mostly regretting it now). 00225 This is to increase compatibility, increase maintainability and facilitate use from other languages. 00226 - C++: ImVec2/ImVec4 do not expose math operators by default, because it is expected that you use your own math types. 00227 See FAQ "How can I use my own math types instead of ImVec2/ImVec4?" for details about setting up imconfig.h for that. 00228 We can can optionally export math operators for ImVec2/ImVec4 using IMGUI_DEFINE_MATH_OPERATORS, which we use internally. 00229 - C++: pay attention that ImVector<> manipulates plain-old-data and does not honor construction/destruction 00230 (so don't use ImVector in your code or at our own risk!). 00231 - Building: We don't use nor mandate a build system for the main library. 00232 This is in an effort to ensure that it works in the real world aka with any esoteric build setup. 00233 This is also because providing a build system for the main library would be of little-value. 00234 The build problems are almost never coming from the main library but from specific backends. 00235 00236 00237 HOW TO UPDATE TO A NEWER VERSION OF DEAR IMGUI 00238 ---------------------------------------------- 00239 - Update submodule or copy/overwrite every file. 00240 - About imconfig.h: 00241 - You may modify your copy of imconfig.h, in this case don't overwrite it. 00242 - or you may locally branch to modify imconfig.h and merge/rebase latest. 00243 - or you may '#define IMGUI_USER_CONFIG "my_config_file.h"' globally from your build system to 00244 specify a custom path for your imconfig.h file and instead not have to modify the default one. 00245 00246 - Overwrite all the sources files except for imconfig.h (if you have modified your copy of imconfig.h) 00247 - Or maintain your own branch where you have imconfig.h modified as a top-most commit which you can regularly rebase over "master". 00248 - You can also use '#define IMGUI_USER_CONFIG "my_config_file.h" to redirect configuration to your own file. 00249 - Read the "API BREAKING CHANGES" section (below). This is where we list occasional API breaking changes. 00250 If a function/type has been renamed / or marked obsolete, try to fix the name in your code before it is permanently removed 00251 from the public API. If you have a problem with a missing function/symbols, search for its name in the code, there will 00252 likely be a comment about it. Please report any issue to the GitHub page! 00253 - To find out usage of old API, you can add '#define IMGUI_DISABLE_OBSOLETE_FUNCTIONS' in your configuration file. 00254 - Try to keep your copy of Dear ImGui reasonably up to date! 00255 00256 00257 GETTING STARTED WITH INTEGRATING DEAR IMGUI IN YOUR CODE/ENGINE 00258 --------------------------------------------------------------- 00259 - See https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/wiki/Getting-Started. 00260 - Run and study the examples and demo in imgui_demo.cpp to get acquainted with the library. 00261 - In the majority of cases you should be able to use unmodified backends files available in the backends/ folder. 00262 - Add the Dear ImGui source files + selected backend source files to your projects or using your preferred build system. 00263 It is recommended you build and statically link the .cpp files as part of your project and NOT as a shared library (DLL). 00264 - You can later customize the imconfig.h file to tweak some compile-time behavior, such as integrating Dear ImGui types with your own maths types. 00265 - When using Dear ImGui, your programming IDE is your friend: follow the declaration of variables, functions and types to find comments about them. 00266 - Dear ImGui never touches or knows about your GPU state. The only function that knows about GPU is the draw function that you provide. 00267 Effectively it means you can create widgets at any time in your code, regardless of considerations of being in "update" vs "render" 00268 phases of your own application. All rendering information is stored into command-lists that you will retrieve after calling ImGui::Render(). 00269 - Refer to the backends and demo applications in the examples/ folder for instruction on how to setup your code. 00270 - If you are running over a standard OS with a common graphics API, you should be able to use unmodified imgui_impl_*** files from the examples/ folder. 00271 00272 00273 HOW A SIMPLE APPLICATION MAY LOOK LIKE 00274 -------------------------------------- 00275 EXHIBIT 1: USING THE EXAMPLE BACKENDS (= imgui_impl_XXX.cpp files from the backends/ folder). 00276 The sub-folders in examples/ contain examples applications following this structure. 00277 00278 // Application init: create a dear imgui context, setup some options, load fonts 00279 ImGui::CreateContext(); 00280 ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO(); 00281 // TODO: Set optional io.ConfigFlags values, e.g. 'io.ConfigFlags |= ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard' to enable keyboard controls. 00282 // TODO: Fill optional fields of the io structure later. 00283 // TODO: Load TTF/OTF fonts if you don't want to use the default font. 00284 00285 // Initialize helper Platform and Renderer backends (here we are using imgui_impl_win32.cpp and imgui_impl_dx11.cpp) 00286 ImGui_ImplWin32_Init(hwnd); 00287 ImGui_ImplDX11_Init(g_pd3dDevice, g_pd3dDeviceContext); 00288 00289 // Application main loop 00290 while (true) 00291 { 00292 // Feed inputs to dear imgui, start new frame 00293 ImGui_ImplDX11_NewFrame(); 00294 ImGui_ImplWin32_NewFrame(); 00295 ImGui::NewFrame(); 00296 00297 // Any application code here 00298 ImGui::Text("Hello, world!"); 00299 00300 // Render dear imgui into screen 00301 ImGui::Render(); 00302 ImGui_ImplDX11_RenderDrawData(ImGui::GetDrawData()); 00303 g_pSwapChain->Present(1, 0); 00304 } 00305 00306 // Shutdown 00307 ImGui_ImplDX11_Shutdown(); 00308 ImGui_ImplWin32_Shutdown(); 00309 ImGui::DestroyContext(); 00310 00311 EXHIBIT 2: IMPLEMENTING CUSTOM BACKEND / CUSTOM ENGINE 00312 00313 // Application init: create a dear imgui context, setup some options, load fonts 00314 ImGui::CreateContext(); 00315 ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO(); 00316 // TODO: Set optional io.ConfigFlags values, e.g. 'io.ConfigFlags |= ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard' to enable keyboard controls. 00317 // TODO: Fill optional fields of the io structure later. 00318 // TODO: Load TTF/OTF fonts if you don't want to use the default font. 00319 00320 // Build and load the texture atlas into a texture 00321 // (In the examples/ app this is usually done within the ImGui_ImplXXX_Init() function from one of the demo Renderer) 00322 int width, height; 00323 unsigned char* pixels = nullptr; 00324 io.Fonts->GetTexDataAsRGBA32(&pixels, &width, &height); 00325 00326 // At this point you've got the texture data and you need to upload that to your graphic system: 00327 // After we have created the texture, store its pointer/identifier (_in whichever format your engine uses_) in 'io.Fonts->TexID'. 00328 // This will be passed back to your via the renderer. Basically ImTextureID == void*. Read FAQ for details about ImTextureID. 00329 MyTexture* texture = MyEngine::CreateTextureFromMemoryPixels(pixels, width, height, TEXTURE_TYPE_RGBA32) 00330 io.Fonts->SetTexID((void*)texture); 00331 00332 // Application main loop 00333 while (true) 00334 { 00335 // Setup low-level inputs, e.g. on Win32: calling GetKeyboardState(), or write to those fields from your Windows message handlers, etc. 00336 // (In the examples/ app this is usually done within the ImGui_ImplXXX_NewFrame() function from one of the demo Platform Backends) 00337 io.DeltaTime = 1.0f/60.0f; // set the time elapsed since the previous frame (in seconds) 00338 io.DisplaySize.x = 1920.0f; // set the current display width 00339 io.DisplaySize.y = 1280.0f; // set the current display height here 00340 io.AddMousePosEvent(mouse_x, mouse_y); // update mouse position 00341 io.AddMouseButtonEvent(0, mouse_b[0]); // update mouse button states 00342 io.AddMouseButtonEvent(1, mouse_b[1]); // update mouse button states 00343 00344 // Call NewFrame(), after this point you can use ImGui::* functions anytime 00345 // (So you want to try calling NewFrame() as early as you can in your main loop to be able to use Dear ImGui everywhere) 00346 ImGui::NewFrame(); 00347 00348 // Most of your application code here 00349 ImGui::Text("Hello, world!"); 00350 MyGameUpdate(); // may use any Dear ImGui functions, e.g. ImGui::Begin("My window"); ImGui::Text("Hello, world!"); ImGui::End(); 00351 MyGameRender(); // may use any Dear ImGui functions as well! 00352 00353 // Render dear imgui, swap buffers 00354 // (You want to try calling EndFrame/Render as late as you can, to be able to use Dear ImGui in your own game rendering code) 00355 ImGui::EndFrame(); 00356 ImGui::Render(); 00357 ImDrawData* draw_data = ImGui::GetDrawData(); 00358 MyImGuiRenderFunction(draw_data); 00359 SwapBuffers(); 00360 } 00361 00362 // Shutdown 00363 ImGui::DestroyContext(); 00364 00365 To decide whether to dispatch mouse/keyboard inputs to Dear ImGui to the rest of your application, 00366 you should read the 'io.WantCaptureMouse', 'io.WantCaptureKeyboard' and 'io.WantTextInput' flags! 00367 Please read the FAQ entry "How can I tell whether to dispatch mouse/keyboard to Dear ImGui or my application?" about this. 00368 00369 00370 HOW A SIMPLE RENDERING FUNCTION MAY LOOK LIKE 00371 --------------------------------------------- 00372 The backends in impl_impl_XXX.cpp files contain many working implementations of a rendering function. 00373 00374 void MyImGuiRenderFunction(ImDrawData* draw_data) 00375 { 00376 // TODO: Setup render state: alpha-blending enabled, no face culling, no depth testing, scissor enabled 00377 // TODO: Setup texture sampling state: sample with bilinear filtering (NOT point/nearest filtering). Use 'io.Fonts->Flags |= ImFontAtlasFlags_NoBakedLines;' to allow point/nearest filtering. 00378 // TODO: Setup viewport covering draw_data->DisplayPos to draw_data->DisplayPos + draw_data->DisplaySize 00379 // TODO: Setup orthographic projection matrix cover draw_data->DisplayPos to draw_data->DisplayPos + draw_data->DisplaySize 00380 // TODO: Setup shader: vertex { float2 pos, float2 uv, u32 color }, fragment shader sample color from 1 texture, multiply by vertex color. 00381 ImVec2 clip_off = draw_data->DisplayPos; 00382 for (int n = 0; n < draw_data->CmdListsCount; n++) 00383 { 00384 const ImDrawList* cmd_list = draw_data->CmdLists[n]; 00385 const ImDrawVert* vtx_buffer = cmd_list->VtxBuffer.Data; // vertex buffer generated by Dear ImGui 00386 const ImDrawIdx* idx_buffer = cmd_list->IdxBuffer.Data; // index buffer generated by Dear ImGui 00387 for (int cmd_i = 0; cmd_i < cmd_list->CmdBuffer.Size; cmd_i++) 00388 { 00389 const ImDrawCmd* pcmd = &cmd_list->CmdBuffer[cmd_i]; 00390 if (pcmd->UserCallback) 00391 { 00392 pcmd->UserCallback(cmd_list, pcmd); 00393 } 00394 else 00395 { 00396 // Project scissor/clipping rectangles into framebuffer space 00397 ImVec2 clip_min(pcmd->ClipRect.x - clip_off.x, pcmd->ClipRect.y - clip_off.y); 00398 ImVec2 clip_max(pcmd->ClipRect.z - clip_off.x, pcmd->ClipRect.w - clip_off.y); 00399 if (clip_max.x <= clip_min.x || clip_max.y <= clip_min.y) 00400 continue; 00401 00402 // We are using scissoring to clip some objects. All low-level graphics API should support it. 00403 // - If your engine doesn't support scissoring yet, you may ignore this at first. You will get some small glitches 00404 // (some elements visible outside their bounds) but you can fix that once everything else works! 00405 // - Clipping coordinates are provided in imgui coordinates space: 00406 // - For a given viewport, draw_data->DisplayPos == viewport->Pos and draw_data->DisplaySize == viewport->Size 00407 // - In a single viewport application, draw_data->DisplayPos == (0,0) and draw_data->DisplaySize == io.DisplaySize, but always use GetMainViewport()->Pos/Size instead of hardcoding those values. 00408 // - In the interest of supporting multi-viewport applications (see 'docking' branch on github), 00409 // always subtract draw_data->DisplayPos from clipping bounds to convert them to your viewport space. 00410 // - Note that pcmd->ClipRect contains Min+Max bounds. Some graphics API may use Min+Max, other may use Min+Size (size being Max-Min) 00411 MyEngineSetScissor(clip_min.x, clip_min.y, clip_max.x, clip_max.y); 00412 00413 // The texture for the draw call is specified by pcmd->GetTexID(). 00414 // The vast majority of draw calls will use the Dear ImGui texture atlas, which value you have set yourself during initialization. 00415 MyEngineBindTexture((MyTexture*)pcmd->GetTexID()); 00416 00417 // Render 'pcmd->ElemCount/3' indexed triangles. 00418 // By default the indices ImDrawIdx are 16-bit, you can change them to 32-bit in imconfig.h if your engine doesn't support 16-bit indices. 00419 MyEngineDrawIndexedTriangles(pcmd->ElemCount, sizeof(ImDrawIdx) == 2 ? GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT : GL_UNSIGNED_INT, idx_buffer + pcmd->IdxOffset, vtx_buffer, pcmd->VtxOffset); 00420 } 00421 } 00422 } 00423 } 00424 00425 00426 API BREAKING CHANGES 00427 ==================== 00428 00429 Occasionally introducing changes that are breaking the API. We try to make the breakage minor and easy to fix. 00430 Below is a change-log of API breaking changes only. If you are using one of the functions listed, expect to have to fix some code. 00431 When you are not sure about an old symbol or function name, try using the Search/Find function of your IDE to look for comments or references in all imgui files. 00432 You can read releases logs https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/releases for more details. 00433 00434 (Docking/Viewport Branch) 00435 - 2024/XX/XX (1.XXXX) - when multi-viewports are enabled, all positions will be in your natural OS coordinates space. 15845 } 15846 15847 // Search for the monitor with the largest intersection area with the given rectangle 15848 // We generally try to avoid searching loops but the monitor count should be very small here 15849 // FIXME-OPT: We could test the last monitor used for that viewport first, and early 15850 static int ImGui::FindPlatformMonitorForRect(const ImRect& rect) 15851 { 15852 ImGuiContext& g = *GImGui; 15853 15854 const int monitor_count = g.PlatformIO.Monitors.Size; 15855 if (monitor_count <= 1) 15856 return monitor_count - 1; 15857 15858 // Use a minimum threshold of 1.0f so a zero-sized rect won't false positive, and will still find the correct monitor given its position. 15859 // This is necessary for tooltips which always resize down to zero at first. 15860 const float surface_threshold = ImMax(rect.GetWidth() * rect.GetHeight() * 0.5f, 1.0f); 15861 int best_monitor_n = -1; 15862 float best_monitor_surface = 0.001f; 15863 15864 for (int monitor_n = 0; monitor_n < g.PlatformIO.Monitors.Size && best_monitor_surface < surface_threshold; monitor_n++) 15865 { 15866 const ImGuiPlatformMonitor& monitor = g.PlatformIO.Monitors[monitor_n]; 15867 const ImRect monitor_rect = ImRect(monitor.MainPos, monitor.MainPos + monitor.MainSize); 15868 if (monitor_rect.Contains(rect)) 15869 return monitor_n; 15870 ImRect overlapping_rect = rect; 15871 overlapping_rect.ClipWithFull(monitor_rect); 15872 float overlapping_surface = overlapping_rect.GetWidth() * overlapping_rect.GetHeight(); 15873 if (overlapping_surface < best_monitor_surface) 15874 continue; 15875 best_monitor_surface = overlapping_surface; 15876 best_monitor_n = monitor_n; 15877 } 15878 return best_monitor_n; 15879 } 15880 15881 // Update monitor from viewport rectangle (we'll use this info to clamp windows and save windows lost in a removed monitor) 15882 static void ImGui::UpdateViewportPlatformMonitor(ImGuiViewportP* viewport) 15883 { 15884 viewport->PlatformMonitor =
